Subject E.P. David et al - Letter from Captain Dewar Durie.

Made by D. S. I. Logan. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

Reference letter dated October 4, 1940,
from Captain Dewar Durie, British Military Liaison
Officer, British Consulate-General, requesting
information concerning 10 persons whose names
appear on attached list, enquiries have been made
by the Special Branch as follows, viz :-

(1) E.P. David is employed in the Secretarial
and Accounting Department of the China
Engineers, 88 Museum Road. His name was
formerly Geir but was legally changed to the
present form, i.e., David. There is no
record of this person in Municipal Police
files.

(2) R.C. Chand - Nothing is known concerning
this individual.

(3) E.A. Cooke - (Eurasian) Employed by
Imperial Chemical Industries (China) Ltd.,
in the Sales Department. Has been a member
of the S.M. Police (Specials) since 1934.
Is known as a quiet living individual who
does a lot of physical training. Nothing
detrimental to his character in municipal
Police records.

(4) R.H. Cunio - Employed by Lowe, Bingham
& Matthews. Nothing unfavourable to his
character known to the Municipal Police.

SUBJECT: Confidential communication dated 27-6-41 from the British Consulate-General concerning Mr. E.N. Pankoff.

Elijah Nikifirovich PANKOFF, naturalized Chinese citizen of Russian origin, was born on July 29, 1896 at Sebastopol, Russia. An ex-officer of the Imperial Russian army he is reported to have served in the Russian Air Force stationed at the Black sea during the Great war and was attached to the French Military Mission in Siberia during the civil war in Russia ( 1918-1919 ). He left Russia for Manchuria in 1919 and for the following three years resided in Harbin reportedly working as a taxi-driver.

From 1925 to some time in 1929 he served as a mechanic in the Aviation Corps of Marshal Chang Tso Ling's army in Mukden and from 1929 to 1938 in a similar capacity in the units of the Nanking Government army stationed in Tsingtao. Some time in 1938 he arrived in Shanghai and in September of the same year proceeded to Australia where he intended to obtain employment in a certain aircraft factory. Being unsuccessful in this ( reportedly, on account of Trade Union regulations ) he returned to Shanghai on 8-1-39 aboard the s.s. "Mellor". Early in March of the same year he applied at the French Consulate-General for a visa to enable him to proceed to Chungking via Hanoi with a view to offering his services to the Chungking government. Apparently he abandoned this plan and soon afterwards secured the position of a mechanic in the French Fire Brigade. Dear Bourne,

We used to have a man on our staff in Tientsin
by the name of D. G. J. Keet and I rather want to get a line
on him. I am not sure whether he is in Shanghai now but he
has been here off and on during the past year or so because
he came to me for recommendations for potential jobs, first
with the I.C.I. and later as broadcaster for XCDN. So far
as I know he did not land either of the jobs and he may still
be here.

If it is not breaking all rules I should be very
glad to have a report on him, particularly regarding his
affiliations at the present time. I say this because he used
to have a most peculiar circle of friends of all nationalities
in Tientsin and he is a most gifted linguist of somewhat unstable
character.

Yours sincerely,
Ivan Tavell.

Major K. H. Bourne, M.C.,

SUBJECT: Wilhelm STERN - Austrian Jewish refugee -
Communication from the British Embassy.

Wilhelm STERN, German (Austrian)
Jewish refugee, born at Vienna on April 11,
1915, arrived in Shanghai in the ss. Felix
Roussel on January 27, 1939.
While employed with Hicem (Far Eastern
Central Jewish Central Information Bureau) Mr.
J. R. JONES of Messrs. Ellis & Hays recommended
him to this office in a communication dated
January 13, 1940 which stated that STERN was
formerly a lieutenant in the Austrian Artillery
and that he had good technical education and
qualifications and that in October 1939 STERN
had registered himself as a volunteer for service
in the British Army.
STERN recently submitted an application
to this office for immigration papers on behalf of
his father and uncle now domiciled in Vienna. In
this application STERN claimed that he earned $600
per month as a musician in a night club. He was
requested to furnish proof in this respect but so
far has not done so. He was also asked why, if
he were earning $600 per month, he desired a
post as a doorkeeper which surely could not pay
such a high salary. His answer was non-committal.

Yen An Fu or Yen Song Chao ( 言嵩岳 ),
age 35, native of Shanghai, was employed as a
2nd Class Clerk by the S.M. Police from September 1,
1930 to November 7, 1931, when he was invalided
under medical certificate.

Since leaving the S.M.P. Yen has been
employed by a number of foreign firms as a clerk
and interpreter, in 1934 he was accused of
misappropriation but the complainant declined to
prosecute.

The notepaper of the Italian Bank for
China on which Yen made his application for
employment to the British Embassy was obtained
from a friend, he is not connected in any way with
the bank and the paper was probably used because
it appeared to him to be impressive. Yen is known
to be slightly mentally deranged.

Subject Bruno GOLDMANN, Czechoslovakian Jewish refugee.

Made by D.S.I. Fitts Forwarded by C.D.I. Tabrum

Bruno GOLDMANN, Czechoslovakian Jewish
refugee, born at Moravia Ostrava on October 14,
1910, arrived in Shanghai from Europe via Siberia
in the ss. Hoten Maru on August 16, 1940. A single
man of considerable personal charm, GOLDMANN resides
at 50/1285 Avenue Joffre with his brother.

The following is a brief summary of
his curriculum vitae:

Five years (1910-1915) elementary schooling at
Moravska Ostrava, seven years (1915-1922) secondary
schooling - passed leaving examination, five
years Prague Polytechnic, electro-mechanical
department, finished with the two requisite
State examinations and graduated with the
equivalent degree of Bachelor of Science (Electrical
Engineering).

Practical experience includes one year (1928)
in workshops of AEG Berlin (testfield, machine
wiring, switchboard mounting, light and power
installations); four years (1929-1933) sales
engineering for D. Bercovitz & Son, Berlin, agents
of Weston Instruments Co., Cambridge Instruments;
Koch & Sterzel, Dresden, Julien Meyer, Prague,
representing several concerns of French nationality
manufacturing laboratory apparatus, measuring
instruments, centrifuges, etc., etc; six years
(1933-1939) production supervisor of the Philips
Radio Set Factory in Prague, managing the departments
of technical preparation and scheduling of production
procuring and storing of materials with full
responsibility for the scheduled output of the
company. Left this position as a result of the
economical and political changes within Czecho-
slovakia after the German invasion. On his way
to the Far East was caught in Poland by the war
there and the subsequent Russian invasion. Managed
to leave Poland in August 1940 and arrived in
Shanghai on August 16 of the same year.

Is able to speak, read and write fluently English,
French, Czech and German and has more than a
passing knowledge of Dutch, Polish and Russian.

GOLDMANN is a member of the Czech Circle
in Shanghai, a pro-Allied organization officially

Subject Lawyer Augustus NEVILLE - British subject

Made by D.S.I. Pitts Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

The following details are submitted in regard
to Lawyer Augustus NEVILLE, British subject by birth.

Born at sea near Singapore in the British ss.
Flintshire on April 18, 1892. Son of Henry James
NEVILLE who was a well-known business men in Japan
and later a contractor for the old Russian Government.
For fifteen years the father was agent in Harbin for
Lloyds of London.

D. W. Neville was privately educated in Japan.
The standard of this education can be considered high.
In 1910 he proceeded to the United Kingdom with his
parents and for two years thereafter was employed with
the concern of Messrs. Babcock & Wilcox, Engineering
experts. In 1912 he proceeded to Russia with his
parents and quickly secured a post as English correspond-
ent with the Sisert Mining District Co. Ltd., with
offices in the Ural Mountains and St. Petersburg.
Later he was employed with the New Cotton Mills concern
in St. Petersburg.

In 1915, after the outbreak of the Great War, he
made his way to the United Kingdom where he joined
the Royal Flying Corps as a 2nd Class Mechanic. Showing
exceptional ability he was able to secure his wings and
by 1917 had gained a commission in the R.F.C. In
1917 he proceeded to Russia as a Second-Lieutenant in
the R.F.C. but in the following year returned to
England as a flying instructor.

现提交关于出生即为英国臣民的律师奥古斯都·内维尔的详细情况。

1892年4月18日出生于新加坡附近海面上的英国轮船“弗林特郡号”（Flintshire）上。父亲亨利·詹姆斯·内维尔（Henry James NEVILLE）是日本著名的商人，后来成为旧俄国政府的承包商。父亲曾在哈尔滨担任伦敦劳合社（Lloyds of London）代理人长达十五年。

D. W. 内维尔在日本接受私人教育。其教育水平可视为很高。1910年，他随父母前往英国，随后两年受雇于巴布科克和威尔科克斯公司（Messrs. Babcock & Wilcox），这是一家工程专家公司。1912年，他随父母前往俄国，并很快在西瑟特矿区有限公司（Sisert Mining District Co. Ltd.）谋得英文通讯员一职，该公司在乌拉尔山脉和圣彼得堡设有办事处。后来，他受雇于圣彼得堡的新棉纺厂公司（New Cotton Mills concern）。

1915年，第一次世界大战爆发后，他前往英国，加入皇家飞行队（Royal Flying Corps）担任二级机械师。由于表现出非凡的能力，他得以获得飞行员资格，并于1917年在皇家飞行队获得委任。1917年，他以皇家飞行队少尉身份前往俄国，但次年以飞行教官身份返回英国。

      In August 1918 while flying over enemy lines
in France he was shot down by anti-aircraft fire. He
escaped into Belgium and was hiding in Brussels
for seven weeks before he got back to England by
way of Holland.
      In April 1919 he was sent to the Vladivostock
Command of the British Forces in Russia in charge
of General (?) Knox as Russian and Japanese liaison
officer. At this juncture it should be pointed
out that Neville has a fluent command of both
Russian and Japanese. He also served in the
same capacity at Russian Island, Vladivostock to
Colonel Sir Edward Grogan.
      Later he was sent to European Russia where
he was attached to the British Railways' Mission as
liaison officer. Took part in the retreat of
Kolchak's armies and in December 1919 was taken
prisoner by the Bolsheviks. Spent eleven months
in various prison camps before being repatriated
to England in December 1920. He was demobilized
in May 1921.
      In 1921 he went to Harbin to join his father
who was acting as Lloyds' agent in that town.
Shortly after his arrival there he was sent to Outer
Mongolia where he remained for one year assisting in
the recovery of furs and pelts.
      In 1922 and 1923 he acted as a technical
engineering adviser to the Peking Medical Union
College in Peiping.

    Late in 1923 he rejoined his father in
Harbin. He stayed in Manchuria until 1938
when it became evident that it was impossible to
carry on business in the face of continued Japanese
expansion and threats. He came to Shanghai
and as he had gained for himself a more than

took up a partnership in World News Photos, 635

    A man of considerable ability Neville is
regarded highly in local photographic circles.
He has a pleasant demeanour, is a good "mixer"
and can hold his own in any circle.

    Neville's wife, Mrs. Alice Louise Julia
NEVILLE (maiden name ELSHOLZ), was born in St.
Petersburg. Although she was born a German
subject her forebears had resided in Russia for
a continuous stretch of 100 years and she
can be regarded or could be regarded as being
more Russian than German. She and her husband
have been married 27 years, the wedding having
taken place in St. Petersburg in 1913.

    Mrs. Neville has definitely no German
connections. Three children have been born of
this marriage, the eldest son Dwyer James Neville,
now 21 years of age, at present being a private
in the 1/Seaforth Highlanders in which he enlisted
in Shanghai.

Made by D.F.S. Killingbeck Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

With reference to the attached enquiry
concerning George G. HOYES, it would appear, from
enquiries made that the man concerned is named
HOYER and not HOYES.

George G. HOYER, aged 19 years, is at present
employed by Messrs. Mollers Ltd. as a radio operator
on the ss "Ariadne Moller". He has been in this
employment only since the beginning of the current year,
but his step-father, H.G. Hoyer, has been employed by
Mollers for some considerable time. Hoyer Junior,
who received most of his education at the French
Municipal College, was accepted by his present
employers without recommendation, as this is his first
position of any consequence. He is stated to have made
attempts at one or two other occupations, but only
served for a matter of a few days in each, stating
that he would only be content in employment as a
radio operator. It would appear that he is an
irresponsible type of youth who has not yet settled
down to any serious employment and who has yet to
prove himself worthy of any position of trust.

The actual father of George G. Hoyer is a person

With reference to the attached communication regarding Captain Paul Herbert Wernberger, enquiries have failed to reveal anything that is very definite concerning the activities of this man.

He arrived in Shanghai on August 28, 1938 and is registered with the International Committee for the relief of European refugees in Shanghai. Records on file with this Committee show that Wernberger, who was born in Vienna on November 18, 1894, is somewhat of a linguist, speaking, besides his mother tongue, English, French and Serbian. He is believed to have been of the Jewish faith, but during June or July of this year, was converted to the Roman Catholic religion and is at present living in the Regina Pacis Catholic Home in Nanzing Road.

He does not appear to be engaged in any regular business or employment in Shanghai, but occasionally does small odd jobs for the Catholic fathers in Hongkew.

As far as the so-called Austrian Committee is concerned, nothing is known amongst prominent local Austrians concerning this organisation. It is possible that this committee has been organised by comparatively recent arrivals in Shanghai and may be conducted on the same lines as the Central Austrian Committee in London and Paris. This large organisation, which is headed by Prinz von STAHREMBERG and composed of officers of the former Austrian army, has as its primary object the restoration of the Austrian Monarchy. 关于所附有关保罗·赫伯特·韦尔恩伯格上尉的函件，经调查未能发现
关于此人活动的任何确切信息。

他于1938年8月28日抵达上海，并在上海欧洲难民救济国际委员会登记。
该委员会存档记录显示，韦尔恩伯格于1894年11月18日出生于维也纳，
略通语言，除母语外，还会说英语、法语和塞尔维亚语。
据信他原信奉犹太教，但在今年六月或七月期间，
改宗罗马天主教，目前居住在南京路的平安天主教之家（Regina Pacis Catholic Home）。

他在上海似乎没有从事任何固定的商业或职业活动，但偶尔
为虹口的天主神父做一些零碎杂活。

至于所谓的奥地利委员会，在当地知名的奥地利人中，无人知晓
该组织的存在。该委员会可能是由近期抵达上海的人员组建，
其运作方式可能与伦敦和巴黎的中央奥地利委员会相同。
这个大型组织由施塔亨贝格亲王（Prinz von STAHREMBERG）领导，
成员包括前奥地利军队军官，其主要目标是恢复奥地利君主制。
